reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates longer, consistent runs at an easy pace, which is crucial for building aerobic base and endurance – key components of trail running speed. Plan B, while prioritizing recovery and form, relies heavily on short, repeated easy runs, which may not provide the stimulus needed for significant speed improvements. Plan A’s inclusion of cross-training also offers a valuable opportunity to build strength and prevent overuse injuries, something Plan B lacks.  Ultimately, Plan A’s structure is more directly aligned with the goal of increasing running volume and developing the necessary aerobic capacity for faster trail running.
